name: REGEXREPLACE
description: REGEXREPLACE replaces text that matches a regular expression pattern with new text. It is more powerful than SUBSTITUTE because it can match patterns rather than fixed strings.
tldr: REGEXREPLACE searches text for a pattern and replaces matching parts with new text.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The original text or cell reference.

parameters.name: regular_expression
parameters.description: The RE2 pattern to find in the text.

parameters.name: replacement
parameters.description: The text to replace matches with. Use $1, $2, etc. to refer to capture groups.

basicExample.description: Remove all digits from a product code
basicExample.explanation: The pattern \d matches any digit. Replacing all digits with an empty string removes them.

advancedExamples.title: Reformat a phone number
advancedExamples.explanation: Capture groups grab the area code, prefix, and line number. The replacement string uses $1, $2, $3.

advancedExamples.title: Remove extra whitespace
advancedExamples.description: Replace multiple consecutive spaces with a single space
advancedExamples.explanation: \s+ matches one or more whitespace characters. Replacing with a single space normalizes spacing.

howItWorks: REGEXREPLACE scans the text for all matches of the pattern and replaces each match with the replacement string. The replacement can include references to capture groups using $1, $2, etc. It uses RE2 regex syntax.

howToSteps.name: Select the text
howToSteps.text: Choose the cell or string to modify.

howToSteps.name: Define the pattern
howToSteps.text: Write a regular expression matching the text to replace.

howToSteps.name: Write the replacement
howToSteps.text: Use literal text or $1, $2 for capture groups.

limitations: REGEXREPLACE is Google Sheets only. Excel has no built-in regex replacement function.
It uses RE2 syntax, which lacks some advanced regex features like lookahead/lookbehind.
Replacement is global; there is no built-in option to replace only the first match.
Special characters in the replacement string may need escaping.

commonErrors.cause: The regular expression is invalid or uses unsupported syntax.
commonErrors.fix: Validate the regex and use RE2-compatible patterns.

commonErrors.cause: The pattern does not match the text.
commonErrors.fix: Test the pattern with REGEXMATCH first to ensure it matches.

commonErrors.cause: Capture groups are not defined or the replacement syntax is wrong.
commonErrors.fix: Use parentheses in the pattern and $1, $2 in the replacement string.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: REGEXREPLACE is exclusive to Google Sheets. Excel users can use SUBSTITUTE for fixed strings, Power Query, or VBA for regex replacement.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: For fixed-string replacement in Excel, use SUBSTITUTE. For pattern replacement, use Power Query or VBA.

faq.question: Can REGEXREPLACE replace only the first match?
faq.answer: No, it replaces all matches by default. To replace only the first match, you need a workaround or script.

faq.question: Can I use REGEXREPLACE in Excel?
faq.answer: No, Excel has no built-in regex replacement. Use SUBSTITUTE for fixed text or VBA/Power Query for patterns.

faq.question: How do I reference capture groups in the replacement?
faq.answer: Use $1, $2, etc. For a literal dollar sign, use $$.

faq.question: Can I use REGEXREPLACE with ARRAYFORMULA?
faq.answer: Yes, wrap it to apply the replacement to a whole range at once.
